label: a1-choice / S1-belief signal, strongest at D2; rises with unrewarded streaks at D1/GO
terms: (phase == D2) * (action == 1) ;; (phase == D2) * (belief - 0.5) ;; (phase != D2) * (belief - 0.5) ;; (phase == D1) * (prev_state == 1) ;; (phase == D1) * ((prev_reward == 0) + (tv("prev_reward", -1) == 0) + (tv("prev_reward", -2) == 0)) ;; (phase == GO) * ((prev_reward == 0) + (tv("prev_reward", -1) == 0) + (tv("prev_reward", -2) == 0)) ;; (phase == D2) * (prev_reward == 0) ;; (phase == D2) * (action == 1) * (prev_reward == 0)
explanation: Raw reset gate r of unit 26. Timing alone gives R^2 0.93 (low at D1 ~0.10-0.15, high at GO ~0.80-0.85, D2 ~0.18-0.28, rising over the episode). Beyond timing, the main driver is an S1/a1 side signal that is largest at D2: higher when the choice just made was a1 (+0.14 at D2) and graded with the ideal-observer belief that S1 is good (D2 weight 0.15 per unit of belief-0.5; about 0.05 at D1/GO). At D1 it is also higher when the previous trial reached S1 (+0.05), and at D1 and GO it rises with the number of unrewarded trials among the last three (+0.03 per miss at D1, +0.04 at GO), so long losing streaks push it up. At D2 a missed previous reward slightly lowers it, more so after an a1 choice. The reached state at D2 adds nothing beyond the choice. No future variables used. Test R^2 beyond timing 0.79 (dev 0.80), against an all-observed ceiling of 0.89 and an all ceiling of 0.91. An earlier explanation used the model policy; the policy-decile table alone scores 0.57, and the observed choice at D2 plus belief do better, so dropping model outputs loses essentially nothing. Remaining misses: D2 after a1 S2 r is over-predicted and D1 after a1 S1 u is under-predicted.

issues: I reproduced the reported test R^2 beyond timing exactly (0.7866). Every term pulls its weight. Dropping each one in turn on test gives: D2 a1 0.677, D2 belief 0.715, non-D2 belief 0.755, D1 prev_state==S1 0.753, D1 miss count 0.772, GO miss count 0.754, D2 prev unrewarded 0.777, D2 a1 x prev unrewarded 0.783.

The D2 choice and the D2 belief are partly redundant. Choice alone scores 0.43, belief alone 0.58, both together 0.61. Together with a raw belief-decile table that alone reaches 0.64, this means belief carries more of the D2 signal than the a1 choice does. The label's 'a1-choice' framing slightly overstates the choice's own contribution.
The claim that the reached state adds nothing at D2 holds. Adding (phase == D2)*(state == 1) gets weight -0.01 and leaves test R^2 unchanged (0.786).

The streak claim holds only at D1 and GO. Swapping in a 4-trial miss count, a consecutive-run length or run^2 changes test R^2 by less than 0.002. At D2 an unrewarded previous trial LOWERS the gate, so the label's unqualified 'rises with unrewarded streaks' is slightly loose.

There is a systematic miss the explanation does not model: D2 after a rare-rewarded a1 S2 r trial is over-predicted by -0.088, the largest error cell in misses. It persists with every variant I tried until I added a dedicated D2*last_is('a1 S2 r') term (weight -0.089), which lifts test R^2 to 0.804.

D1 after an unrewarded S1 trial is under-predicted (+0.043 for a1 S1 u in misses; profile residual +0.092). An interaction (phase == D1)*(prev_state == 1)*(prev_reward == 0) fixes part of this and raises test R^2 to 0.797. Its weight is +0.06, larger than the main D1 prev_state==S1 effect (+0.025), so most of the D1 'reached S1' effect actually comes from unrewarded S1 trials.
The remaining gap to the all-observed ceiling is about 0.09 (0.79-0.80 vs 0.89). No single large error class remains: per-phase mean errors are within 0.014 and all other cells are within 0.05.
